A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core arguments, experiments, and Appendices A–C. Text, equations, figures, and tables are readable; reformatting and renumbering do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original interpolation, probing, and steering experiments using Gemma-3-4B and MetaCLIP-2.

after.justification: v2 retains original steering and probing experiments and additionally reports covariance-approximation errors in Table 1.

M1.justification: The dual-steering objective, probe constructions, and regularized Newton update in Algorithm 1 are retained. Algorithm 2 specifies conjugate gradient for the previously unspecified linear solve; this implementation disclosure does not establish a change to the underlying steering method.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4 contexts for verb-form and English-to-French steering, synthetic color/shape images, and COCO object concepts. The appendix retains the same concept coverage; the new approximation test introduces no distinct dataset or task.

E2.justification: Euclidean steering remains the comparator, evaluated alongside dual steering with both Primal MD and Dual MD probes. Newly cited manifold-steering and concept-erasure methods are discussed but are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 1 introduces an approximation-evaluation protocol using Frobenius matrix error, K values of 1, 20, 2000, 20000, and 200000, and trajectory steps 0, 5, 10, 50, and 100. Existing data selection, steering metrics, and the 0.9999 stopping threshold are retained; the threshold was already documented in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds a top-K sensitivity check against the full Fisher information matrix in Table 1, quantitatively testing an approximation whose accuracy v1 only asserted. The existing regularization-geometry and probe-assumption analyses in Appendix C remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and SEM across test contexts using the same per-path probability-binning procedure, moved from v1 Appendix B.2 to v2 B.3. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The quantitative robustness trajectories are substantively revised, particularly LLM rank differences. For English-to-French steering with Dual MD, Euclidean rank difference changes from an early plateau near 0.54 in v1 Figure 4 to a gradual rise exceeding 0.6 in v2 Figure 5; corresponding appendix trajectories also change in Figures 10 and 11, respectively. Table 1 additionally reports approximation errors, including values rounding to 0.0000 for K at least 20000. These are revised reported results, not an established performance improvement.

T1.justification: Sections 4.2 and B.2 add a computational-complexity argument contrasting explicit covariance computation and solution, O(kd² + d³), with conjugate gradient, O(nKd) after top-K truncation. The interpolation proposition, concept-factorization definition, steering theorem, and Appendix A proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: information geometry for softmax representations, distinct primal/dual interpolation semantics, and dual steering that minimizes off-target disturbance under the stated assumptions. The principal empirical controllability claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly distinguishes the factorization assumption needed for the theorem from steering differences observed without it. Section 5.3 replaces v1's explicit explanation of possible target-steering failure and increased off-target distortion with an emphasis on empirical outperformance despite assumption violations. Appendix C.2 retains the evidence of probe mismatch.

D1.justification: Algorithm 2 and Appendix B.2 newly detail matrix-free conjugate gradient, suggest 20 iterations, and provide residual stopping and numerical safeguards. The top-20000 approximation, regularization value 0.005, data-processing instructions, and code-access link were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds focused discussion of concurrent manifold steering by Sarfati and Wurgaft and concept-erasure work by Bolukbasi, Vargas, Belrose, and Ravfogel. It also distinguishes Singh's affine steering using L2 distance from the paper's output-distribution KL objective. The broader novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with limited terminology and explanatory edits. Appendix B gains a separate Metrics subsection, the stopping-rule paragraph moves within it, and v2 adds an Impact Statement and expands implementation and related-work passages.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the main text into a two-column conference layout, changes typography and figure sizing, and rearranges displays throughout the paper and appendices. It adds the primal/dual-space schematic in Figure 4, Table 1, and Algorithm 2; existing figures are retained and renumbered rather than removed.

improvement.justification: Algorithm 2 improves implementation reproducibility, while Table 1 quantitatively supports the approximation-accuracy assertion already present in v1. The expanded research positioning and geometric illustration also help. These targeted gains outweigh the softened failure discussion in Section 5.3, although Appendix C.2 still documents the violated probing assumption. The revised numerical curves alone do not establish improved empirical quality.
